title: A-N-H
hookLine: anah, to answer, and ani, the poor or humble

lines: A SOFT ANSWER TURNETH AWAY WRATH.
cards: Someone snaps at you. A text in capitals, a remark across the table, a customer who's had a long day and decided you're the reason. You have about one second before you answer.
Proverbs has a line for that second: "A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger." The Hebrew for answer there is ma'aneh, from the root ayin, nun, hey.
Read those letters another way, and they give a word for someone poor, low, bowed down. An answer, and a humble person.

teach.b: A-N-H. Ayin, nun, hey. First, to answer: anah, the everyday verb for replying, and also for God answering.

teach.h: ANI: THE POOR ONE IS HEARD.
teach.b: A psalm says: "This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him." The word for poor there is ani, written with the same letters. It isn't the ani that means I; that one starts with a different letter, alef.
This ani is the lowly one, with nothing to bargain with. And the psalm says that one is heard. Second, humility.
From the same letters comes anav, humble, and anavah, humility.
The Torah uses it for Moses, of all people, the leader who spoke with God: "Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth." Meek there is anav.
The text doesn't call him the smartest or the strongest. It calls him the humblest. Third, the honest part.

teach.h: TWO ROOTS, OR ONE? READERS DIFFER.
teach.b: Dictionaries often list answering and being lowly as two separate roots that share letters; whether they were ever one word is a question for linguists. So the link isn't a hidden code.

teach.h: THE SOFT ANSWER IS THE HUMBLE ONE.
teach.b: But some readers hear them together, and the pairing teaches something: the soft answer is the humble answer. It doesn't need to win, or arrive with a speech prepared. It answers the way Moses led, from low down.
And the psalm adds the other side: the one who is low is the one whose cry gets answered.

how: Jewish ethical teaching prizes anavah, humility, and holds up Moses as its model from Numbers 12:3; Proverbs' 'soft answer' is a common Jewish guide for replying in a quarrel.

o: the Hebrew root of answering, and of the humble
the Hebrew root of I, speaking of myself
the Hebrew root of anger and quarreling

p: an answer, a soft one turns away wrath
the poor one, who is heard

s: the ani that means poor is the same word as ani, I
I starts with alef. the poor one starts with ayin.
the Torah calls Moses very meek
everyone agrees answer and humble come from one root
dictionaries often list them as two roots sharing letters. some readers hear them together anyway.

games.q: someone snaps at you across the table. you have one second. what does Proverbs suggest?
games.why: "a soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger." the word for answer, ma'aneh, is from A-N-H.

practice: Bring to mind a reply that's waiting, an email drafted in your head, an argument still warm, and notice the answer you want to give, the one that wins.

Let it sit for a breath, then look for a lower one that leaves room for the other person, maybe starting with you might be right, or tell me more. If you pray, you can bring that person into your prayer.

wordCard.voice: A-N-H. Ayin, nun, hey: anah, to answer; ma'aneh, an answer; ani, the poor one; anav, the humble. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: humble, the word used for Moses, in Numbers 12:3.

carryVoice: Your line: answer humbly. The soft answer never needs the last word. See you tomorrow.
